title: Bayern Munich win Bundesliga title: Vincent Kompany’s attacking juggernaut is a team for the ages
author: Sebastian Stafford-Bloor
content:
Bayern Munich have won the German Bundesliga for the 13th time in 14 seasons with their 4-2 victory over Stuttgart on Sunday.

Bayern were afforded the opportunity to win the title after second-placed Borussia Dortmund lost 2-1 at Hoffenheim on Saturday, with Vincent Kompany’s side requiring one point to take an unassailable lead. Stuttgart took an early lead at the Allianz Arena, only for goals from Raphael Guerreiro, Nicolas Jackson, Alphonso Davies and Harry Kane helping secure the home side’s win, with the away team scoring a late consolation.

The win moves Bayern 15 points clear of Dortmund after another dominant league campaign in which they have scored 109 goals, 40 more than any other team, while holding the strongest defensive record by conceding just 28. The previous highest-scoring side in the Bundesliga was Bayern in 1971-72, when they scored 101 goals across that league season.

With their 35th German title, Bayern have furthered their status as Germany’s most successful club — 26 clear of Nuremberg (nine titles), the next most successful club.

Vincent Kompany’s side also remain in contention to win the Champions League for the first time since 2020, and will face holders Paris Saint-Germain in the semi-finals after knocking out 15-time winners Real Madrid. They will face Bayer Leverkusen in the semi-finals of the DFB-Pokal.

Kompany also won the Bundesliga crown with Bayern in his first season at the helm in 2024-25, which was his first top-flight silverware having also led Burnley to the Championship title in 2022-23. The Belgian was appointed after Bayer Leverkusen won the 2023-24 title, the only Bundesliga in the 14 most recent editions that Bayern did not win.

Analysis by German football correspondent Sebastian Stafford-Bloor

This has been a magnificent season for Bayern. Occasionally in the past, their title wins have reflected their opponents’ inability to challenge, more than their own excellence. But, while a threat never really emerged from Dortmund this season and RB Leipzig and Leverkusen remain in transition, that should not detract from what Kompany’s team have been able to accomplish.

A half-century-old record from 1972 has gone. Previously, the most goals scored during a single season was 101, set by Bayern themselves. This team have obliterated it. They reached and exceeded it on Matchday 29, with five games left to play, and by the time this season is over the new benchmark will likely be unreachable for a generation at least.

There is evolution all over the pitch — individually and collectively. Kane has played the football of his career this season, growing to become not just a goalscorer or a playmaker, but of fundamental importance in every area of the game. Within this team, he has become a legitimate, strong contender for the Ballon d’Or.

The attack around him, as that goalscoring record suggests, has been sensational. The addition of Luis Diaz has proven a masterstroke, adding a missing element to a forward line that now, perhaps, is the most dangerous in Europe.

Serge Gnabry has been fantastic; a player revived from a mid-career slump. Michael Olise has been sensational and has been elevated to become the best player in his position, anywhere in the world.

Together, they have proven lethal.

The individual improvements are no less striking. Konrad Laimer, previously a utility player, has been fashioned into one of the best full-backs in Europe. Aleksandar Pavlovic, so prominent in the recent Champions League elimination of Real Madrid, is delivering on his long-held promise and the suggestion that, in the coming years, he’s capable of becoming an era-defining player.

The Bundesliga creates an unhelpful context sometimes. Are Bayern that good or is everyone else just incapable of matching them? Is the outcome just the result of the financial inequities that lie within German football? This year, no: Bayern have been outstanding and have been far more than the sum of their parts.

The most points they have ever accumulated in a league season is 91, set during the treble-winning year under Jupp Heynckes in 2012-13. Bayern have now moved on to 79 points, with 12 left to play for and with every chance of equalling that record.

This is a special team. A side for the ages.

Analysis by tactics and data writer Anantaajith Raghuraman

This Bayern team will go down as an offensive juggernaut built on three prongs: versatility, efficiency and tactical fluidity.

Their front four, which has been devoid of the talented Jamal Musiala for large stretches, is at the centre of it all.

Kane has been the best player in Europe, with 50 goals and the ability to pop up all over the pitch. Serge Gnabry’s work-rate and passing have been exemplary.
Out wide, Luis Diaz’s tireless off-the-ball movement and Michael Olise’s passing arsenal have added several dimensions to this team.

Lennart Karl is a bright prospect and Aleksandar Pavlovic’s abilities in and out of possession — recently evidenced in the 4-3 win over Real Madrid — have continued to improve. In his 11th season, Joshua Kimmich remains central to their build-up play as the graph below shows.

Kompany’s side have scored 109 times from 91.8 expected goals, an overperformance of 17.2, the highest across Europe’s top five leagues this season.

They have managed an xG per shot of 0.16, a shot accuracy of 45 per cent and shot-to-goal conversion rate of 19 per cent. All of those are the highest by a team in Europe’s top five leagues across a full season since 2019-20 (PSG managed a higher xG per shot in 2019-20 but the season concluded early due to COVID-19).

They are also the only team across the top five leagues this season to attempt more than seven penalties and not miss any. Bayern are 11-for-11 from the spot.

All of that suggests that their goalscoring, while historic, is not merely a statistical anomaly. Bayern are getting into excellent positions and taking their chances.

Bayern can hurt you in multiple ways as the graph below shows.

Across Europe’s top five leagues, no team has scored more goals from fast breaks (defined by Opta as a shot attempt created at speed after a team wins the ball in their own half) than Bayern’s 12. It is also the most by a team in the last six Bundesliga seasons, with four rounds still to go.

Only Manchester City (14) have more goals from sequences of nine or more passes than Bayern’s 13. Their 4.3 through-balls attempted per 90 is the most by any team in Europe’s top five leagues since 2019-20.

They have also scored 14 times from corners, with only two teams (Arsenal and Inter on 16) recording more in 2025-26.

As their playstyle map below shows, Bayern lead Europe in multiple attacking and creative metrics.

The offensive dominance has not come without a few drop-offs defensively. As the map above shows, set-piece defending has been an issue. Bayern have also made 30 errors leading to a shot (including 10 goals), the most by a Bundesliga team since 2019-20. Their 1.1xG against per 90 is an increase on the 0.8xGA from 2024-25.

Few can argue, though, that the risks taken have paid off handsomely on the other end. A second treble in six years – and third in 13 – is achievable for one of the most dominant European teams ever.
